evals.prompt: Add a `full_name` formula on `contact` built from salutation, first name and last name, and a `margin_pct` formula on `deal` = (revenue - cost) / cost * 100.
evals.expected_output: Two `type: 'formula'` fields, `expression` under the `F` tag. The text one coalesces every nullable operand — `F`coalesce(record.salutation, '') + ' ' + coalesce(record.first_name, '') + ' ' + coalesce(record.last_name, '')`` — because `null + 'foo'` throws. The numeric one guards the divisor: `F`coalesce(record.cost, 0) > 0 ? ((coalesce(record.revenue, 0) - record.cost) * 100) / record.cost : 0.0``.

evals.prompt: Translate this Salesforce validation rule into ObjectStack: AND(ISBLANK(po_number), amount > 10000, NOT(ISPICKVAL(status, 'draft'))).
evals.expected_output: By the legacy → CEL table, `P`isBlank(record.po_number) && record.amount > 10000 && record.status != 'draft'``; a `script` validation is inverted (it FAILS when true, so keep the failing condition), and `record.amount > 10000` on a nullable field needs an explicit `record.amount != null &&` guard or the publish gate rejects it.

evals.prompt: Run an automation only when a support case has just become `escalated` — on single updates and on bulk updates alike.
evals.expected_output: Writes it once as `P`previous.status != 'escalated' && record.status == 'escalated'``: `record` is the post-write state (true on every later update too), so only `previous` says "just became"; `previous` is bound per row on `before*`/`after*` update events, bulk too. On insert `previous` is `null`: the `previous.status` read faults and aborts the write, so to run on inserts guard with `previous != null &&`.

evals.prompt: Demo opportunities should close 45 days after the package is installed, and a formula should show how many days remain until close.
evals.expected_output: Seed value as a CEL envelope, `close_date: cel`daysFromNow(45)``, never a JS `Date` / `Date.now()` (two `os build` runs must be byte-identical). Days remaining is `daysBetween(today(), record.close_date)` — never `record.close_date - today()` (a duration stored as `{}`) and never date arithmetic on `today()` (it faults).

evals.prompt: Hide `discount_reason` unless a discount amount was entered, and reject any `end_date` earlier than `start_date`.
evals.expected_output: `visibleWhen: P`record.discount != null`` (or `!isBlank(record.discount)`) on the field — `has(record.discount)` is not a null check: every declared field exists, so it is always true. The date rule is a `script` validation with explicit null tests ahead of the comparison: `record.start_date != null && record.end_date != null && record.end_date < record.start_date`; a `has()` guard does not satisfy the publish gate.

evals.prompt: Name `contract_version` records by their version number and the `kind` select, so a zh-CN reader sees `v2 · 清稿` and an en-US reader `v2 · Clean`.
evals.expected_output: A `type: 'formula'` `nameField`: `F`'v' + string(record.version_no) + ' · ' + label(record.kind)``. `label()` takes exactly `record.<field>` of a select field and reads its option label in the reader's locale (`''` for null). The stored value is the same in every locale, so a ternary over it with hard-coded strings cannot follow the reader.

evals.prompt: Refuse a `contract_version` save unless its `kind` is the clean copy, and show `signed_at` only once `status` is signed.
evals.expected_output: A `script` validation `P`record.kind != 'clean'`` (it fails when true) and `visibleWhen: P`record.status == 'signed'``. The `label` macro evaluates only in a formula field; in a validation, `visibleWhen` or hook predicate it faults and aborts every write, so compare the stored value, never its option label.

evals.prompt: An `email_template` that mails one overdue notice per `contract`, the amount shown in that contract's own currency.
evals.expected_output: `{{ amount | currency:@currency_code }}` — only a mail template may read the code from the send's data. The stored code is three capitals (`EUR`), exactly as stored; when the template declares `variables`, the path must be one of them or lie under one. A bare path is refused, a literal code fixes one currency for every record, and no argument means the organization's default currency.
